notes: Inbound via self-serve signup -> converted to lead after free-credit usage. Small devtools startup building a VS Code extension + web IDE feature set. Wants hosted API for speed to market; likely to remain on hosted for 6-12 months then reassess Dedicated. Key asks: long context (>32k ideal, open to chunking/embeddings), streaming low-latency token-by-token responses for code edits, SDKs for Node/Typescript and Rust (also Python), granular per-user/per-tenant rate limits, client key rotation guidance, and transparent per-token cost breakdown. Security: SOC2 desirable, audit logging required for enterprise customers down the road. Very price sensitive — startup budget, wants predictable monthly cap during POC. Quote from founder on discovery call: "We need p95 interactive latency under ~200ms for short completions; long context queries can be async but should return in <2s for 10-20k token lookups." Uses hybrid retrieval: chunked embeddings + rerank for large repos. Trying to avoid model drift; asks about model pinning and snapshotting for reproducible completions. Interested in auto-fallback if capacity constrained (fall back to smaller cheaper model) but worried about API compatibility. Asked for guidance on batching vs streaming tradeoffs since extension does many small interactive calls. Also asked about web-client auth patterns and rotating keys for end-user accounts. POC plan: integrate hosted API into VS Code extension (background process), run 2-week internal beta with 50 power-users, measure latency p50/p95, and monitor token spend. If POC successful, goal is to convert to paid hosted tier and revisit Dedicated in 12 months.
